subject: Re: Renewal — benchmark request & pricing gap analysis
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@cartnexus.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Kyle Morgan <kyle.morgan@cartnexus.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal — initial heads-up

Rishi,

Thanks for the renewal quote you sent last week. We've been asked to review everything end-to-end by procurement — BigCloud circulated a counterproposal this morning that is materially cheaper at scale and includes an ops-managed migration offer. Procurement wants two things from Redwood before they move forward:

- A short benchmark that shows performance (latency/tokens/sec) for our typical 1–2k token chat workloads vs the competitor on the same hardware profile
- A clear concession roadmap: what pricing, committed capacity, or SLA credits you'd offer to bridge the gap

I've attached our renewal roll-up and the competitor term sheet for context (CartNexus_Renewal_Rollup.pdf).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can run the benchmark and get me a proposal by mid-Nov? If you need a PoC environment or specific traffic samples, let me know.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
VP Product Operations — CartNexus

[attachment: CartNexus_Renewal_Rollup.pdf (pdf)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@cartnexus.com>
Cc: Kyle Morgan <kyle.morgan@cartnexus.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal — initial heads-up

Hi Alicia — thank you for the heads-up and the rollup. We can absolutely run the benchmark and put together a graded concession roadmap.

High-level plan:
- Neha will run a focused benchmark against a matching instance profile (we'll use your anonymized sample traffic) and provide a short report (latency percentiles, tokens/sec, mem/KV behavior).
- We'll produce two commercial options: (A) a capacity-focused renewal with 12–24 month committed GPUs + token discount and (B) a migration-facilitation offer (credits + paid migration support) if you choose to move to a lower-cost runtime.

Next steps: a quick 30-min call Monday to confirm traffic samples and success metrics. Neha / Marissa — can you join? Alicia, is 10am PT Monday OK?

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: CartNexus — benchmark + concession ask (urgent)

Team — running this thread to coordinate. CartNexus has a competitor offer in play and procurement wants evidence + concessions by mid-Nov. Details: attached renewal rollup from Alicia.

Ask:
- Neha: need a lean benchmark plan (24–36 hour run) that replicates their typical mix: 70% chat, 25% short completions, 5% embeddings. Target devices: A100-equivalent. Provide a test script, expected metrics, and a quick template report. Can you also estimate delta if we enable 4-bit quantization?
- Marissa: commercial options — can we propose a 15–20% committed-volume discount with a 12–24 month term, plus a 3-month migration credit if they need to switch to a cheaper variant? Also confirm if we can offer a 99.9% token-generation SLA for the top tier.

Timeline: bench deliverable by Nov 6, commercial by Nov 9, customer review by Nov 12. Procurement may escalate to execs if we miss.

Thanks — R

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 14:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: CartNexus — benchmark + concession ask (benchmark plan + attachments)

Rishi / Marissa — plan below and attachments included.

Summary of approach:
1) Test harness: run a controlled 24-hour run with a representative 10k request sample (redacted) derived from Alicia's rollup. Pattern: bursty chat (most common), long context (1–2k tokens) for 15% of sessions.
2) Metrics captured: p50/p90/p99 generation latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory footprint, KV-hit ratios.
3) Comparison targets: Redwood on our L50 inference profile vs BigCloud-specified instance. We'll normalize per-GPU.
4) Quantization: run baseline FP16 and a 4-bit static quant profile; report delta on p90 & tokens/sec to evaluate cost/quality tradeoff.

Attachments: benchmark-instructions.txt (test steps), perf-report-template.xlsx (report skeleton).

Risk notes:
- If the customer expects identical end-user outputs, this is not a functional correctness bakeoff — it's purely performance/cost. Any quality differences should be surfaced separately and tied to evaluation prompts.
- Migration credits and SLA commitments need quota and legal approval from Marissa / contracts.

I'll stand up the harness on Nov 4 and share results by EOD Nov 6.

- Neha
Senior SRE, Inference Performance

[attachments: benchmark-instructions.txt, perf-report-template.xlsx]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@cartnexus.com>
Cc: Kyle Morgan <kyle.morgan@cartnexus.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal — benchmark request & pricing gap analysis (proposal)

Alicia / Kyle — thanks for the time last week. Attached is our benchmark proposal and a commercial counteroffer (CartNexus_Benchmark_Proposal.pdf, revamped_offer_v2.pdf). Summary below:

Benchmark: concise 24-hour run that will replicate your production mix; Neha will deliver a short report (p50/p90/p99, tokens/sec, utilization) and an appendix with quantization impact. Expected delivery: EOD Nov 11.

Commercial counteroffer (high level):
- Option A (Committed capacity): 18-month term, 20% token discount after a 6-month ramp, priority scheduling windows during peak runs, and 2 additional reserved GPUs for heavy-event windows.
- Option B (Migration facilitation): 12-month term, 12% token discount, $75k migration credit (applied as service credits), and 3 dedicated migration days from our solutions team.
- SLA: we can commit to 99.9% token-generation availability for Option A. In addition, we'll include a $50k one-time credit if we fail to hit the SLA in a quarter (subject to contract language).

Next steps: if this looks acceptable, we can schedule the benchmark run and lock a small canary for migration planning. If procurement needs deeper pricing movement, Marissa is willing to discuss further adjustments tied to expanded multiyear commitments.

Best,
Rishi

[attachments: CartNexus_Benchmark_Proposal.pdf, revamped_offer_v2.pdf]

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@cartnexus.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Kyle Morgan <kyle.morgan@cartnexus.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal — benchmark request & pricing gap analysis

Rishi — thank you for the quick turnaround and the proposal. A few notes from procurement after an initial pass:

1) The credits are appreciated but procurement is pushing for a deeper first-year discount (they want closer to 25% on committed volume).
2) They want a binding migration facilitation SLA in Option B (defined deliverables and deadlines), not just credits.
3) Can you confirm the benchmark will include a token-level cost model (per 1M tokens) post-quantization? That will be a key comparison point against BigCloud's numbers.

We'd like to set a 30-minute exec call next week with your SVP of Sales to iron out the remaining gaps if possible. Procurement indicated they'll escalate if we don't see movement.

Appreciate the speed — Alicia
